title: I built a romance visual novel where an LLM writes every page live. Here's how it works, what each page costs, and what broke.
author: Defiant-Mood6717
selftext:
I'm the dev of Monte Lua, a browser visual novel set in a small seaside town. The cast, sprites, backgrounds and music are fixed and made ahead of time. The story itself is written live: every page is new, and you can either press Continue or type what you do. It's been running with real players for a few months, so here's what I've learned, in case it's useful to anyone building something similar.

**Text and staging are separate jobs.** One call writes a whole page of prose (about 1,300 words, ~30 beats). A second, cheaper model then reads that page and answers multiple-choice questions for every beat: which background, who's on screen, which expression, which music, any screen effect. Two things surprised me. Putting hundreds of questions in one call gave the same answers as splitting them up, at half the cost, because you pay for the repeated context. But trimming the option text did hurt: when I cut options down to short ids, agreement dropped by about 30%. The model only knows an option by its words.

**Pictures for the big moments.** A small model writes a brief, and the image model draws it with reference images of the characters. The worst bug was characters swapping roles (A hugging B came out as B hugging A). The cause was my prompt: the references were labelled with bare names. Labelling each reference with the character's look, and repeating that look the first time they're mentioned, fixed most of it. Outfits drifting turned out to be the story text inventing jackets and cardigans, not the image model.

**Long stories need summaries, and caching matters more than the summary.** Some saves are past 12,000 beats, so the history gets compacted into a summary at a size limit. This week I found that the summary call used a different reasoning setting from the story calls, so it never hit the prompt cache: 28 of the last 30 missed. With the setting matched, the first run was 97% cached and cost $0.25 instead of $0.40.

**Rough costs:** about $0.04 per page of text and $0.05 per picture.

**What I removed:** an agent loop that planned the story (too slow for someone waiting on the next page) and character voice TTS (it can't read the room, so every line sounds slightly wrong, which breaks the spell faster than silence).

Curious how others handle consistency over very long runs, and whether anyone has an image model that keeps two or three characters straight from references reliably.

It's free to start if you want to see it: https://montelua.ai
